info.name: SLT_Resources_Collection
info.description:
RES-009 (05_RESOURCE_MGMT, FR-15) — material request submit-then-approve via Newman.

Run:
  newman run fieldops/src/test/postman/SLT_Resources_Collection.json \
    --env-var baseUrl=http://localhost:8080 \
    --env-var techToken=<technician JWT> \
    --env-var adminToken=<admin JWT> \
    --env-var materialId=<an active material with stock>

NOTE ON THE ENDPOINT AND STATUS CODE: the sheet writes POST /api/material-requests and
POST /api/material-requests/{{reqId}}/approve, and expects 201 on submit. The implemented routes
are POST /api/inventory/material-request (singular) and
POST /api/inventory/material-requests/{{reqId}}/approve (InventoryController), and the submit
returns 200 OK, not 201 Created — unlike this codebase's other create endpoints. The submit body is
also multi-item ({items:[{materialId, quantity}], taskId, faultId, urgency, notes}), so there is no
top-level materialId/quantity. This collection drives the real routes and asserts 2xx on submit
rather than a literal 201.

Approval requires notifyRequester:true for the requester to be told; the Admin portal
(InventoryPage.js) sends it, so the collection does too.

newman is not installed in this environment and nothing listens on :8080, so this collection cannot
produce a verdict here. Its executable twin is
fieldops/src/test/java/lk/slt/fieldops/controller/SltResourcesCollectionTest.java, which asserts
exactly the same things through MockMvc against the real database.
